cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Pick the Prize
cards.instruction: Make them choose which reward, principle, or relationship matters most when not everything can be kept.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our anniversary table and your trophy ceremony are both at seven. Please choose which booking I should keep.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The ceremony finishes at eight. We can eat afterwards.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The kitchen closes at eight. That's a cancellation, not a later sitting; please don't enter it as both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave the ceremony at half seven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even if your name hasn't been called? Put that departure in your calendar now, or tell me to cancel dinner. We need one plan we can actually follow.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 corrects later dinner into cancellation and A5 supervises the departure commitment, making professional schedule management force a value choice.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 ceremony ends at kitchen close; A3 excludes after; B4 offers early departure and A5 tests leaving before own name.

relationship.evidence: B2/B4 try to keep both events through plausible scheduling changes.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 compromise to reveal the reward that may be forfeited.
